transliteration_key.g: ق في العراقي (تُلفظ كالجيم القاهرية) / گ

reply.english: And blessed Eid to you too

phrases.arabic: وين چنت؟ ليش ما جيت تعيّد وياانا؟
phrases.transliteration: ween chint? leesh maa jiit t3ayyid wiyyaana?

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Blessed Eid, uncle!

dialogue.speaker: Uncle Hassan
dialogue.arabic: وعيدكم مبارك، كل عام وانتو بخير
dialogue.english: And blessed Eid to you, may you be well every year

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: And you too, may you see it again next year

dialogue.speaker: Uncle Hassan
dialogue.english: And you too. Please, come in

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Thanks, what is this lovely smell?

dialogue.speaker: Uncle Hassan
dialogue.arabic: كليچة العيد، أم حسن سوتها من أمس
dialogue.transliteration: kleechat il-3eed, umm 7asan sawwatha min ams
dialogue.english: Eid cookies, Umm Hassan made them since yesterday

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: God give her strength! Can I take one?

dialogue.speaker: Uncle Hassan
dialogue.english: Take as many as you want

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Where are the kids?

dialogue.speaker: Uncle Hassan
dialogue.english: They went to pray the Eid prayer, they will be back now

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: وأنا لازم أروح أزور ستي، وعدتها أجيها اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana laazim aroo7 azoor sitti, wa3adit-ha ajiiha il-yoom
dialogue.english: And I have to go visit my grandma, I promised her I would come today

dialogue.speaker: Uncle Hassan
dialogue.arabic: روح الله وياك، وسلّم عليها وعيدها مبارك
dialogue.transliteration: rooH allaa wiyyaak, w-sallim 3aleeha w-3eedha mubaarak
dialogue.english: Go, God be with you, greet her and blessed Eid to her

pair.english: May you be well every year

response.english: And blessed Eid to you too

pair.english: May you see it again next year

lessons.culture: On the first day of Eid Iraqis greet with "عيدكم مبارك" and "كل عام وانتو بخير", and visiting relatives, above all the elders, is expected. Children get an "عيدية", and homes fill with "كليچة", the date or walnut cookies that are the Iraqi Eid sweet.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "عيد مبارك". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: Correct and polite, but in Iraqi speech "بيك" is used, not "فيك".

exercises.tip: Iraqi says "بيك" (in you) where formal Arabic says "فيك"; to a woman it is "بيچ".

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "عساكم من عوّاده". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: This is a long formal wish that is heard in sermons, not in daily talk.

exercises.tip: "عسى" gives the wish "may it be so"; you send the same wish back.

exercises.prompt: كل عام وانتو ____

too_formal.feedback: The formal form says "أنتم"; Iraqis say "انتو".

exercises.tip: "بخير" here means in good health and happiness.

exercises.prompt: دا ____ هدوم العيد الجديدة

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal word; Iraqis say "ألبس" and call clothes "هدوم".

exercises.tip: "دا" before a verb means it is happening right now.

exercises.prompt: Translate: Blessed Eid to you all

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal, written way of wishing it.

exercises.tip: The ending "-كم" means "you all".

exercises.prompt: Translate: We visited my grandma today

too_formal.feedback: The word "جدتنا" is formal; in Baghdad a grandmother is often "ستي".

exercises.tip: "ستي" is a warm everyday word for my grandmother.

exercises.prompt: What do children get from adults at Eid?

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal word that nobody says in the street.

exercises.tip: The "عيدية" is usually money, given on the first day of Eid.

exercises.prompt: Which is the famous Iraqi Eid cookie?

too_formal.feedback: The word "الكعك" is used in other countries; in Iraq the Eid cookie is "كليچة".

exercises.tip: The "چ" is pronounced like the "ch" in "cheese".

exercises.prompt: Arrange: We're going to the Eid prayer

too_formal.feedback: The word "ذاهبون" is formal; Iraqis say "رايحين".

exercises.tip: "رايحين" means going, and "احنا" (we) can be left out.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: Why didn't you come to celebrate Eid with us?

too_formal.feedback: The words "لماذا" and "لم" are formal; Iraqis say "ليش ما".

exercises.tip: "وياانا" means "with us".

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.english: Ramadan kareem, Umm Ali

dialogue.speaker: Umm Ali
dialogue.english: God is more generous, come in

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: احنا اليوم معزومين عندچ على الفطور، صحيح؟
dialogue.english: We are invited to you for iftar today, right?

dialogue.speaker: Umm Ali
dialogue.english: Yes, I have been preparing since the morning

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.english: What did you make?

dialogue.speaker: Umm Ali
dialogue.arabic: سويت تمن وگيمة وشوربة عدس، وبعد الفطور زلابية
dialogue.transliteration: sawweet timman w-gayma w-shoorba 3adas, w-ba3d il-fuTuur zalaabya
dialogue.english: I made rice, qeema stew and lentil soup, and zalabia after iftar

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: الله يعطيچ العافية. الفطور اليوم الساعة شگد؟
dialogue.transliteration: allaa y3Tiich il-3aafya. il-fuTuur il-yoom is-saa3a shgadd?
dialogue.english: God give you strength. What time is iftar today?

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.arabic: أني صايمة من الفجر وهسة تعبت شوية
dialogue.transliteration: ani Saayma min il-fajir w-hasa t3ibit shwayya
dialogue.english: I have been fasting since dawn and now I am a bit tired

dialogue.speaker: Umm Ali
dialogue.english: Just a little left, the cannon will fire soon

dialogue.speaker: Zaynab
dialogue.english: May God accept our fasting

lessons.culture: In Ramadan Iraqis say "رمضان كريم", answered with "الله أكرم", and families often invite each other to iftar, a "عزيمة". Baghdad has a tradition of the iftar cannon, and a typical iftar table has soup, rice and stew, and sweets such as zalabia.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "رمضان كريم". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: This is a correct formal wish, but the set reply to this greeting is "الله أكرم".

exercises.tip: The greeting says Ramadan is generous; the reply says God is more generous.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "الله يتقبل صيامكم". Reply.

too_formal.item: تقبل الله منا ومنكم صالح الأعمال
too_formal.feedback: This is a long formal reply heard in speeches, not in daily talk.

exercises.tip: It means "from us and from you", sending the wish back.

exercises.prompt: احنا ____ من الفجر

too_formal.feedback: The word "صائمون" is formal; Iraqis say "صايمين".

exercises.tip: "صايمين" means fasting, for we or you all.

exercises.prompt: الفطور اليوم الساعة ____؟

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis ask "الساعة شگد".

exercises.tip: The Iraqi "گ" is a hard "g" sound, spelled with the letter "ق" in formal Arabic.

exercises.prompt: Translate: We're preparing for iftar

too_formal.feedback: The word "الإفطار" is formal; Iraqis say "الفطور".

exercises.tip: "دا" makes it happening right now.

exercises.prompt: Translate: The iftar cannon fired

too_formal.feedback: This is the formal passive; Iraqis say it with "انضرب".

exercises.tip: "انضرب" is the Iraqi "was struck", used for a cannon firing.

exercises.prompt: What is the meal before dawn called?

too_formal.feedback: This is a descriptive formal phrase, not the word people use.

exercises.tip: "سحور" is eaten before the fast starts at dawn.

exercises.prompt: Which greeting is answered with "الله أكرم"?

too_formal.feedback: "رمضان مبارك" is a fine greeting too, but it gets a different reply.

exercises.tip: The generous greeting gets the "more generous" reply.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: Whose invitation are you at tonight?

too_formal.feedback: The word "مدعو" is formal; Iraqis say "معزوم".

exercises.tip: "منو" means who, and "معزوم" means invited to a meal.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: We started fasting from dawn

too_formal.feedback: The word "بدأنا" is formal; Iraqis say "بدينا".

exercises.tip: "بدينا" means we started.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: مبروك يا نور، سمعت أخوچ راح يتزوج!
dialogue.transliteration: mabrook ya noor, smi3it akhooch raa7 yitzawwaj!
dialogue.english: Congratulations Noor, I heard your brother is getting married!

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.english: God bless you, may it be your turn next

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: God willing. When is their wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: يوم الخميس الجاي، وهسة دا يجهزون للعرس
dialogue.transliteration: yoom il-khamiis ij-jaay, w-hasa daa yjahhzuun lil-3urs
dialogue.english: Next Thursday, and now they are preparing for the wedding

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: Who is invited?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.english: The whole family, the neighbours and the friends

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: God make them happy. How is the stage?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: الكوشة مزينة مرة حلوة، ورد أبيض وذهبي
dialogue.transliteration: il-kuusha mzayyna mara 7ilwa, ward abyaD w-dhahabi
dialogue.english: The stage is decorated very beautifully, white and gold flowers

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: And what did the bride wear?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: لبست فستان أبيض، شكلها مثل القمر. وانت شنو هدية جبتلهم؟
dialogue.transliteration: libsat fustaan abyaD, shikilha mithil il-gamar. w-inta shinu hidiyya jibitilhum?
dialogue.english: She wore a white dress, she looks like the moon. And what gift did you bring them?

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.english: I brought them a nice set of glasses

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.english: God keep you, they will surely like it

pair.english: May it be your turn next

lessons.culture: Iraqi weddings are big family events, with the couple seated on the "كوشة", a procession called the "زفة", and the line dance "چوبي" for the guests. A single friend is met with "عگبالك", and the usual reply is "إن شاء الله".

exercises.prompt: A friend says to you at a wedding: "عگبالك". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but formal; the everyday reply is "إن شاء الله".

exercises.tip: "إن شاء الله" (God willing) is the polite reply to any good wish about the future.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "الله يسعدكم". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; people answer with a short blessing like "الله يخليك".

exercises.tip: To a woman it is "الله يخليچ".

exercises.prompt: مبروك ____

too_formal.feedback: The word "الزفاف" is formal; Iraqis say "العرس".

exercises.tip: "عرس" is the everyday word for wedding.

exercises.prompt: الكوشة مزينة ____ حلوة

too_formal.feedback: The word "جداً" is formal; Iraqis say "مرة" for very.

exercises.tip: Here "مرة" means very, not one time.

exercises.prompt: Translate: When is their wedding?

too_formal.feedback: The word "متى" is formal; Iraqis say "شوكت".

exercises.tip: "شوكت" means when.

exercises.prompt: Translate: She wore a white dress

too_formal.feedback: The word "ارتدت" is formal; Iraqis say "لبست".

exercises.tip: "أبيض" (white) does not change here because "فستان" is masculine.

exercises.prompt: What is the wedding stage called in Iraq?

too_formal.feedback: The word "منصة" is formal; Iraqis say "كوشة".

exercises.tip: The couple sits on the "كوشة" during the wedding.

exercises.prompt: Which is the traditional Iraqi line dance done at weddings?

too_formal.feedback: This is a general formal phrase, not the name of the dance.

exercises.tip: The dancers hold hands in a line and step to the drum.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: They're preparing for the wedding

too_formal.feedback: The words "يستعدون" and "للزفاف" are formal.

exercises.tip: "جهّز" means to prepare, and a bride's "جهاز" is her set of household things.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: What gift did you bring them?

too_formal.feedback: The word "ماذا" is formal; Iraqis say "شنو".

exercises.tip: "جبتلهم" is "جبت" (I brought) joined with "لهم" (to them).

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: عيد ميلاد سعيد يا سارة! كل عام وانتي بخير
dialogue.transliteration: 3eed miilaad sa3iid ya saara! kull 3aam w-inti bkhayr
dialogue.english: Happy birthday Sara! May you be well every year

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: God keep you safe, Omar

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: How old did you turn?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: الله يطوّل عمرچ. شنو هدية تريدين؟
dialogue.english: May God lengthen your life. What gift do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: ما أريد شي، بس تجي للحفلة
dialogue.transliteration: maa ariid shi, bass tiji lil-7afla
dialogue.english: I want nothing, just come to the party

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Of course I will come. Are you preparing the cake?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: إي، أمي دا تجهّز الكيكة من الصبح
dialogue.transliteration: ee, ummi daa tjahhiz il-keeka min iS-SubuH
dialogue.english: Yes, my mother has been preparing the cake since the morning

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وسمعت أخوچ ترفّع بشغله، مبروك الترفيع
dialogue.transliteration: w-smi3it akhooch traffa3 b-shughla, mabrook it-tarfii3
dialogue.english: And I heard your brother got promoted at work, congratulations on the promotion

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: الله يبارك بيك، وانت بعد مبروك البيت الجديد
dialogue.transliteration: allaa ybaarik biik, w-inta b3ad mabrook il-beet ij-jidiid
dialogue.english: God bless you, and congratulations to you too on the new house

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: الله يخليچ. وبالحفلة لازم تطفّين الشموع وأنا أصوّر
dialogue.transliteration: allaa ykhalliich. w-bil-7afla laazim iTaffiin ish-shumuu3 w-ana aSawwir
dialogue.english: God keep you. At the party you must blow out the candles and I will film

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: اتفقنا، أشوفك بالحفلة إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: ittifagna, ashoofak bil-7afla in shaa allaa
dialogue.english: Agreed, I will see you at the party, God willing

pair.english: May you be well every year

lessons.culture: Birthday parties with a cake and candles are common in Iraq, especially for children and young people, and "كل عام وانت بخير" and "الله يطوّل عمرك" are the standard wishes. Congratulations on success, a promotion, a baby or a new house get the same reply, "الله يبارك بيك".

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "عيد ميلاد سعيد". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but stiff; friends answer with a short blessing.

exercises.tip: "الله يسلمك" is a warm all-purpose thank you.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "مبروك البيت الجديد". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but Iraqis say "بيك", not "فيك".

exercises.tip: The same reply works for every congratulation in this unit.

exercises.prompt: شگد صار ____؟

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal way to ask someone's age.

exercises.tip: The Iraqi way asks "how much did your age become".

exercises.prompt: الله ____ عمرك

too_formal.feedback: The word "أطال" is formal; Iraqis say "يطوّل".

exercises.tip: This wish is said to someone older, or on a birthday.

exercises.prompt: Translate: Congratulations on the promotion

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal sentence; Iraqis just say "مبروك الترفيع".

exercises.tip: In Iraqi work talk a promotion is often "ترفيع".

exercises.prompt: Translate: Blow out the candles

too_formal.feedback: The word "أطفئ" is formal; Iraqis say "طفّي".

exercises.tip: This is said to one man; to a woman it is "طفّين الشموع".

exercises.prompt: How do you ask a friend how old they turned?

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal way to ask.

exercises.tip: "صار" here means became.

exercises.prompt: Which one means birthday party?

too_formal.feedback: The word "احتفال" is formal; Iraqis say "حفلة".

exercises.tip: "حفلة" is any party.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: We're preparing the cake

too_formal.feedback: The word "الكعكة" is formal or foreign to Iraq; a cake is "كيكة".

exercises.tip: "جهّز" is the everyday word for get ready.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: What gift do you want?

too_formal.feedback: The word "أي" is formal; Iraqis say "شنو".

exercises.tip: "تريد" is the Iraqi word for want.

challenge.title: Congratulate a friend
challenge.instructions: Pick an occasion (Eid, Ramadan, a wedding, a birthday, a baby or a new house) and write a short talk between you and a friend, where you congratulate them and they reply.
required_elements: A greeting or congratulation that fits the occasion you chose
A natural reply to the congratulation
One question about the details, such as when, who or what gift
A blessing such as الله يخليك or عگبالك

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: Congratulations on the baby, Hassan!

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: God bless you, Ali

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.english: What is his name?

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.english: We named him Omar, God keep him

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: الله يخليه ويطوّل عمره. عگبالي إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: allaa ykhalliih w-yTawwil 3umra. 3igbaali in shaa allaa
dialogue.english: God keep him and lengthen his life. May it be my turn, God willing

dialogue.speaker: Hassan
dialogue.arabic: إن شاء الله، تعال زورنا الجمعة
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa allaa, ta3aal zoorna ij-jum3a
dialogue.english: God willing, come visit us on Friday
